document: IV stage 2 — the frontier judge on Bedrock, under amendment 2's registered budget
🔴_the_finding_is_the_checkers: all three checker variants read IDENTICALLY at 0.693 — the same at n=50 (0.60) and at 166 rated pairs. The judge separates the checker from chance (+0.18) and does not separate the checker's variants from each other at all. With 110 of 300 briefs collapsing to a single candidate before the judge was asked, that is one thing said twice: the checker's dimensions do not separate these samples. It caps what this arm can say about selection.
⚠️_the_subset_over-estimated: the 50-brief subset parsed 92.1% and cleared the ≥90% gate that authorised this run; the full 300 parsed 87.4%. The gate worked and the run is usable, but fifty items predicted three hundred and predicted them HIGH — the same shape as the budget error that preceded it.
⚠️_a_failed_run_precedes_this_one: an earlier full attempt at a 128-token budget rated 23 of 300 and was REFUSED by the arm itself: 167 of 190 calls returned an empty text block having spent the whole budget on reasoning. $1.6478. The budget had been sized on six toy pairs rather than on real briefs.

instrument.reading: the budget fixed the judge, not only the parsing — a judge that cannot finish its sentence cannot agree with itself either
instrument.reasoning_cost: AGGREGATE for this run: median ~476 of 1024 output tokens on the real-brief probe, the reasoning being most of it. Per-call reasoning_tokens_est and stop_reason begin with the next run; the transport computed them and the meter did not store them, and a value returned and never stored is not a record.
